reason: Gravity should bring water from the clouds down as rain.
expectation: The cloud droplets will fall as rain, potentially completing the rain goal.

alternatives.reason: Atmospheric heat loss may also matter, but gravity seems more directly related to rainfall.

effect: Rain is falling, but it has not yet completed the goal of reaching the ground.

alternatives.reason: Atmospheric cooling might help rain survive, but the rain is already falling toward the coast.

reaction: The result clarifies that water can cycle back into the air without being lost.
reason: Atmospheric heat loss is the only offered combination and may help rain reach the ground.
expectation: The atmosphere will cool as infrared energy escapes, possibly allowing more rain to reach the surface.

effect: The atmosphere is cooling slowly as energy escapes from its upper layers; rain returning as steam can now be combined with it.
reaction: The coupled cooling of the atmosphere and surface makes the process clearer.
reason: This is the only offered combination, and it may let the recycled water fall again as the atmosphere cools.
expectation: The steam may condense and return as rain, though another step could be needed for it to reach the ground.

effect: The same water is cycling through evaporation and condensation; rain reaching the ground remains the goal.
reaction: The repeated cycling makes clear why the first rain need not form an ocean.
reason: This is the only offered combination; cooler air may help the recycled water condense again.
expectation: Water may form droplets or rain again, though further steps may be needed for it to reach the ground.

effect: Cooling has produced persistent rain that is more likely to survive its descent.
reaction: The link between coupled cooling and rain survival is clear, though the repeated cycling felt somewhat repetitive.
reason: The only offered combination brings the rain to rock cool enough to retain water.
expectation: Rain will reach the cool rock and remain liquid, likely completing the rain goal.

effect: Rain now remains liquid on cool rock, completing the final goal and the chapter.
reaction: It was satisfying to see the earlier cooling make a tangible difference beside the still-hot lava.

mostWorthwhile.text: Cooling the coast and then bringing rain to the cool rock made the contrast between neighboring surface conditions concrete.

leastWorthwhile.text: The sequence of recycling steam through the cooling atmosphere felt somewhat repetitive, even though it reinforced the water cycle.

surprise.text: Rain hitting lava returned as steam without leaving the planet’s water inventory, while neighboring cool rock could retain water.

arbitrary.text: Combining recycled water with cooler air made sense, but the intermediate recycling step felt somewhat mechanical; it was also the only offered action.

continue.text: I would continue: the explanation of uneven cooling and recycled water made me curious how the accumulating water would develop into a sea, although I would hope for fewer repetitive steps.
